summary:
**BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:** Quinbrook is the one capital-segment investor in this corpus that builds the assets itself: a founder-owned, USD 8.95bn (regulatory AUM) value-add manager whose funds developed Supernode — 520 MW / 1,858 MWh operating in Brisbane since 28 July 2026 under Origin tolls, with a 260 MW / 1,216 MWh third stage financed for Stanwell and CATL as supplier across all three — and founded Rowan Digital Infrastructure, the US hyperscale developer in which funds affiliated with Blackstone acquired 'a significant minority stake' on 9 April 2026 (reported, not announced, at 49% and about USD 3.8bn excluding debt). It closed its second UK fund at GBP 587m on 8 July 2026 and is raising a third global flagship, Quinbrook III, with a USD 4bn target that it has announced only in a Companies House filing. It is also the owner of Habitat Energy, whose reported sale process (JLL and Boston Consulting Group, March 2026) has produced no public step in seven months, and whose FY2025 accounts, with those of its UK holding group, were overdue at Companies House on 3 October 2026.

**BACKGROUND.** Founded in 2015 by David Scaysbrook and Rory Quinlan (Capital Dynamics Clean Energy & Infrastructure, Novera Energy), Quinbrook manages five closed funds — Low Carbon Power Fund (2017–19), Renewables Impact Fund (GBP 620m, October 2023), the USD 600m Valley of Fire continuation fund (April 2024; Blackstone Strategic Partners lead), the Net Zero Power Fund (USD 3bn including co-investment, August 2024) and Renewables Impact Fund II (GBP 587m) — plus Quinbrook III in market. Per its 28 July 2026 Form ADV the US adviser reports USD 8,952,975,521 of non-discretionary regulatory assets across 20 accounts; IPE Real Assets ranked it 89th among infrastructure managers (infrastructure AUM EUR 3,632m at 31 December 2024). Brian Restall became its first chief executive in October 2025 under the two founders. Realised exits: Scout Clean Energy to Brookfield (about USD 1bn cash, 2022), 49% of Gemini to APG (2022), Lockyer Energy to Stanwell (2025), Energy Locals to a Palisade consortium (2024), Flexitricity to Drax (GBP 36m enterprise value, completed 31 March 2026). Infrastructure Investor named it Energy Transition Investor of the Year (Global) for 2024.
ecosystemRole: We assess Quinbrook as the capital segment's developer-manager: a challenger by scale beside Blackstone, Brookfield, Macquarie, MGX, BlackRock and KKR, but the only one of them whose funds originate, build and operate the storage and data-centre assets rather than buying platforms. Through its development affiliate Private Energy Partners it is itself the procurer at Supernode — CATL's EnerC Plus and TENER S systems, GE Vernova power conversion, Powerlink connection — and it co-developed the 8-hour EnerQB product with CATL. Its purchase orders therefore sit closer to the manager than at any peer: a storage vendor meets Quinbrook's own team on Supernode Stage 4 and the Gladstone hub, not a portfolio company's. On the data-centre side it founded Rowan (3rd-largest US hyperscale developer by capacity per Altman Solon, cited by Quinbrook) and now shares it with Blackstone; on the optimisation side it owns Habitat Energy, for sale. Its UK franchise — the largest private owner of synchronous condensers, Cleve Hill, Mallard Pass — sells grid stability and contracted power to NESO and corporate offtakers.

productsAndServices.name: Supernode (Brisbane) — Quinbrook-developed BESS campus and hyperscale data-centre precinct
productsAndServices.category: Platform — storage and powered land (developed, owned and operated by Quinbrook funds)
productsAndServices.description: Supernode, at Brendale/South Pine north of Brisbane, is the asset that makes Quinbrook a buyer: 'developed by Quinbrook' with its affiliate Private Energy Partners, held in the Net Zero Power Fund, and registered with AEMO as Supernode BESS (DUIDs SNB01 and SNB02, scheduled bidirectional units, Origin Energy Electricity Limited as intermediary from 17 February 2026). Stage 1 (260 MW / 619 MWh) reached commercial operations on 17 February 2026; Stage 2 completed construction and commenced operations on 28 July 2026, taking the operating campus to 520 MW / 1,858 MWh — 'the largest operating BESS in the National Energy Market' — under 12-year tolling agreements with Origin Energy for 100% of Stages 1–2. Stage 3 (260 MW / 1,216 MWh; Stanwell's release said 250 MW / 1,010 MWh) carries a 15-year offtake with the state-owned Stanwell Corporation signed 16 April 2025 and reached financial close on A$469m of debt on 28 July 2026 (CBA, MUFG, Deutsche Bank, DNB, Rabobank), for completion in 2027. Stages 1–2 were financed with A$722m of debt (January 2025; Bank of America, CBA, Deutsche Bank, Mizuho, MUFG), 'the largest standalone BESS project financing in Australia'; total project financing is about A$1.2bn and Quinbrook states it 'has committed A$1.4 billion to develop the first three stages'. CATL supplies EnerC Plus containers for Stages 1–2 and TENER S for Stage 3 under a long-term service agreement; GE Vernova supplied power conversion and SCADA for Stages 1–2.
highlights: Three stages total about 780 MW / 3,073 MWh (Quinbrook's figures vary between releases: 3,073, 3,074 and 3,096 MWh); the site has 'capacity for a further 520 MW of expansion' and Stage 4 is 'in pre-construction' as the first deployment of EnerQB, the 8-hour product Quinbrook co-developed with CATL (announced 5 March 2025; '>3 GW' planned across Quinbrook's Australian sites)

The data-centre precinct ('Supernode DC', '500 MW-IT potential', three high-voltage grid connections, Torus dark fibre) is labelled 'Construction' on quinbrook.com; no tenant or hyperscale customer is named in any source read
Quinbrook's own portfolio page still labelled Supernode 'Construction' on 7 September 2026 while its text records Stages 1–2 operating

Related Queensland pipeline: an exclusivity MoU with Stanwell (3 December 2025) for the Gladstone SDA Energy Hub — up to 1,080 MW of OCGT with synchronous-condenser capability and 780 MW of 8-hour EnerQB storage — and an EnerQB demonstration at Stanwell Power Station

productsAndServices.name: Rowan Digital Infrastructure — the hyperscale developer Quinbrook founded, now shared with Blackstone
productsAndServices.category: Platform — AIDC development ('Energy Intensive Industry and Industrial Precincts' strategy)
productsAndServices.description: Rowan began in 2020 as a joint venture between Quinbrook and Birch Infrastructure and became 'a wholly owned portfolio company of Quinbrook' when Quinbrook internalised the team in January 2023; it is held in the Net Zero Power Fund. University Pension Plan Ontario completed a co-investment in August 2024 (terms undisclosed). On 9 April 2026 Quinbrook, Rowan and Blackstone announced that 'funds affiliated with Blackstone have acquired a significant minority stake in Rowan'; no party disclosed the percentage, the price or whether the figure was equity or enterprise value. The Information, relayed by IREI and The Tech Capital, reported 49% at a company valuation of about USD 3.8bn excluding debt, with Quinbrook retaining operational control and Blackstone taking significant control rights — those figures are reported, not announced. David Scaysbrook is Rowan's chairman and Kathryn Lin, Quinbrook's digital-infrastructure lead, sits on its board. Rowan describes itself as developing 'multiple 300 MW to 1+ GW campuses across the U.S.' with more than 20 sites, 5.8–6 GW under evaluation and 'over 1.2 GW of leased capacity with leading hyperscale customers'; Quinbrook cites Altman Solon ranking it the third-largest US hyperscale developer by capacity.
highlights: Campuses: Bauxite I–III at Quantum Frederick, Maryland (2,000 acres; 626 MW rising to more than 1 GW of utility load; Bauxite I substantially complete July 2025; USD 975m, 1.2bn and 925m of financings in 2025); Cinco, Lytle, Texas (300 MW near-term, 400 MW secured with AEP; USD 550m construction financing February 2026); Temple, Texas (1,350+ acres, 1.6 GW of power 2026–2030; Temple I 300 MW broke ground March 2026; about USD 2.95bn of green financing closed 27 May 2026, 'the largest financing in the company's history'); campuses in development in Oregon and Virginia
Rowan has raised USD 4.4bn under its Green Finance Framework across three projects in a year and says total debt raised exceeds USD 4bn; CFO Kevin Mammel, CEO Charley Daitch

Politics: three Rowan Frederick LLCs were plaintiffs in the April 2026 suits against a referendum on Frederick County's data-centre overlay zone; the Maryland Supreme Court blocked the referendum on 30 June 2026, but the county executive rejected the neighbouring Quantum Maryland agreement on 15 September 2026 and extended a data-centre moratorium to 1 July 2027 — Rowan's existing campuses sit inside the zone, and the effect on later phases is not stated

Rowan signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge (July 2026), committed USD 38m to Temple water infrastructure (17 September 2026) and published a 'Rowan Community Guarantee' (21 September 2026)

Blackstone's relationship pre-dates Rowan: Blackstone Strategic Partners was lead investor in Quinbrook's USD 600m Valley of Fire continuation fund (April 2024). Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust's Q2 2026 10-Q does not mention Rowan, so the stake is not in that listed vehicle

productsAndServices.name: Habitat Energy — the optimiser for sale — and the UK flexibility franchise (Flexitricity exited, Velox retained)
productsAndServices.category: Platform — storage optimisation and flexible generation (QRIF; 'Flexibility, Firming and Grid Support' strategy)
productsAndServices.description: Quinbrook acquired Habitat Energy Limited on 30 November 2021 (terms undisclosed) and holds it in QRIF through its UK holding group, Renewable and Grid Services Limited (RGS), whose FY2024 accounts carry Habitat's 'Optimisation services' turnover of GBP 4,169,575 (up 80%) within group turnover of GBP 14,227,627 and a group loss of GBP 68.65m; RGS owed GBP 526.8m to the Jersey manager at 31 December 2024 and names Quinbrook Holdings Limited as its ultimate controlling party. Habitat states 5.5 GW under contract across the UK, US and Australia, 130 people, and ranked first in Modo Energy's December 2025 ERCOT table; it kept winning mandates through 2026 (PJM entry in April; Octopus Australia's Fulham and Blind Creek projects in July–August). New Project Media reported on 17 March 2026 that Quinbrook was 'working with JLL and Boston Consulting Group' to sell Habitat; Quinbrook did not comment, no bidder, price, signing or withdrawal has been reported since, and Quinbrook's own Habitat page — labelled 'Operational & Expanding' — has not been modified since 29 August 2025. On 3 October 2026 Companies House showed FY2025 accounts 'overdue' for both Habitat Energy Limited and RGS (due 30 September 2026); the manager's own UK company filed on time. Flexitricity, the Edinburgh aggregator Quinbrook bought in 2020 for GBP 15.2m, was sold to Drax at an enterprise value of GBP 36m (about GBP 42m of proceeds including a GBP 6m working-capital and cash adjustment), announced 21 January 2026 and completed on 31 March 2026 per Drax's half-year accounts, after Ofgem notification and National Security and Investment Act approval. Velox Power — more than 300 MW of UK gas peakers across 52 sites, developed since 2017 — stayed with Quinbrook.
highlights: Quinbrook's side of the Habitat record agrees with the `habitat-energy` dossier on every dated fact (acquisition, mandate report, overdue accounts, board changes); it corrects one: Quinbrook says Flexitricity's contracted portfolio grew 'from 540 MW to c. 1.3 GW', not the ~0.9 GW Drax cited — both figures are recorded

The PSC register of RGS no longer evidences the Jersey holding: a PSC07 of 18 May 2026 ceased Renewables Impact Holding Limited as of 29 November 2021 and a PSC08 of 19 May 2026 states there is no registrable person; the economic chain to QRIF rests on the accounts, not the register

Habitat's board carries five Quinbrook-side directors — Scaysbrook (chairman per Quinbrook's March 2022 release; not restated since), Quinlan, James Allan, Hank Jones (17 June 2025) and Keith Gains (10 December 2025) — and no independent non-executive is disclosed
Any Habitat sale faces the same gates Flexitricity cleared: NSI Act review and Ofgem

productsAndServices.name: UK and Irish grid franchise — synchronous condensers, Cleve Hill, Mallard Pass, Uskmouth, Aegis
productsAndServices.category: Platform — contracted grid stability, solar-plus-storage and transport energy (QRIF and QRIF II)
productsAndServices.description: Quinbrook calls itself 'the largest private owner of synchronous condensers in the UK': Rassau (Ebbw Vale; Pathfinder I, operating since February 2022), the four Thistle units in Scotland (Rothienorman December 2024, Thurso May 2025, Gretna August 2025, Neilston 29 April 2026; Pathfinder II, 'more than half of the GBP 323 million total contract value', 10-year CPI-linked NESO contracts) and the Severn pair (Cilfynydd 2027, Sellindge 2028; Pathfinder III), financed with GBP 120m (April 2024) and GBP 156m (29 April 2026; Standard Chartered, Barclays, Siemens Financial Services); Wexford in Ireland (963 MVA.s, EirGrid Low Carbon Inertia Services contract) was its first Irish investment (July 2025, 100% of the equity, held in QRIF II). Cleve Hill Solar Park in Kent — the UK's first solar NSIP, bought in 2021 as 'Project Fortress' — reached commercial operation on 1 July 2025 at 373 MWdc, the largest operating solar park in the UK, with a 150 MW / 300 MWh battery due in 2026, a 15-year Tesco PPA for 65% of output, a CfD and Shell route-to-market for the rest, a 15-year Capacity Market agreement and GBP 238.5m of debt (Lloyds, NatWest). Mallard Pass (373 MWdc / 240 MWac, the second solar NSIP; acquired 3 February 2025) starts construction in 2026 for a 2028 COD; Uskmouth (230 MW / 460 MWh at a former coal site; E.ON took 50% on 15 March 2025) is due to operate in 2026; Aegis Energy (up to GBP 100m for HGV refuelling hubs) and Project Norton (65 MW solar + 41 MW BESS) are QRIF II holdings.
highlights: Eight condensers operating or under construction supported by 'over GBP 500 million in committed capital'; development partner Welsh Power; three new SPVs (Quinbrook EM1/SE1/SW1 Grid Services) incorporated 14 May 2026
Cleve Hill's contracted and index-linked revenues exceed GBP 480m; BESS up to 350 MW consented
QRIF II's thesis is Clean Power 2030 and Ireland's 80% renewables target; GBP 1.2bn of equity and GBP 1.7bn of total capital invested in UK and Irish projects to date (Quinbrook, July 2026)
productsAndServices.positioning: A UK NSIP-solar and grid-stability specialist whose revenues are NESO contracts, CfDs and corporate PPAs rather than merchant power.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: NESO Stability Pathfinder contracts, CfD, Capacity Market, corporate PPAs; project debt; equity from QRIF and QRIF II.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Cleve Hill BESS 2026; Uskmouth 2026; Mallard Pass construction 2026, COD 2028; Severn condensers 2027–28; Wexford 2027; first Aegis hub 2026.

productsAndServices.name: US solar-plus-storage and realised platforms — Primergy, Gemini, Valley of Fire, GlidePath; exits (Scout, Lockyer, Energy Locals)
productsAndServices.category: Platform — US development and the realisation record
productsAndServices.description: Primergy (Oakland; 100% owned since 2020; NZPF) reports 10.3 GW of solar and 51.5 GWh of storage in development and construction, 1.2 GW and 1.5 GWh operating and more than USD 4bn of financing raised; its flagship Gemini (Clark County, Nevada; 690 MWac / 966 MWdc solar + 380 MW / 1,416 MWh BESS; 25-year NV Energy PPA; COD 2024) was financed with USD 1.9bn of debt and tax equity in April 2022, sold 49% to APG for ABP in October 2022 (price undisclosed) and 51% into the Valley of Fire continuation fund in April 2024, and refinanced in March 2026 with USD 600m of 24-year notes and a USD 160m letter-of-credit facility backed by a 10-year PTC transfer. Other holdings: PurposeEnergy and Junction City Biomethane (US biogas and RNG), Elemental Clean Fuels (Canada; majority stake from the founders and Piney Point Capital, October 2025), Cape Byron Power (two NSW biomass plants) and the Northern Quartz silicon campus in Townsville (development).

strategyRead: **(High confidence)** We assess that **Quinbrook is the one investor in this segment whose own team is the buyer**. Basis: Supernode was 'developed by Quinbrook' with its affiliate Private Energy Partners; the supplier agreements (CATL's EnerC Plus and TENER S; GE Vernova power conversion) and the EnerQB product were signed and announced by Quinbrook itself, not by a portfolio company; the Gladstone hub MoU is Quinbrook's. For a storage or power-conversion vendor, Quinbrook is a procurement counterparty in Australia in a way Blackstone, Brookfield or KKR never are.

**(High confidence)** We assess that **Quinbrook is monetising its two Habitat-era UK optimisers and keeping the hard assets**. Basis: Flexitricity sold to Drax (GBP 36m EV, completed 31 March 2026) with Velox Power explicitly retained; the JLL/BCG mandate on Habitat (New Project Media, March 2026); two sponsor-side board appointments at Habitat in six months. Cuts against: no bidder, price or signing has surfaced in seven months, Habitat kept winning mandates, and its FY2025 accounts are late — the sale may have stalled rather than progressed. Collection gap: Quinbrook has never acknowledged the process.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **the Blackstone entry into Rowan is a recapitalisation of a developer that outgrew its fund, not a partial exit from a position Quinbrook wants to leave**. Basis: Rowan raised about USD 4.4bn of debt in a year and 'over 1.2 GW of leased capacity'; Quinbrook kept the chairmanship and a board seat; Blackstone Strategic Partners was already the lead investor in Quinbrook's 2024 continuation fund. The 49% and about USD 3.8bn ex-debt figures are The Information's, confirmed by no party; the equity basis (not EV) is how the report framed them. Treat the valuation as reported.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Quinbrook III (USD 4bn target) is the firm's bet that the NZPF record — Supernode delivered, Rowan recapitalised, Gemini refinanced — sells a flagship twice the size of the last**, and that the thin FY2025 at parent level (Jersey-group profit USD 1.56m against USD 22.79m; a first bank charge over the UK manager) reflects fundraising costs ahead of fees. Basis: the UK accounts' strategic report; the Form D first sale of USD 30m; the July 2026 UK holding company. Cuts against: no press release and no target close date; USD 30m sold nine months in.

**(Moderate confidence)** We assess that **Quinbrook's governance is founder control under a new CEO layer**: the founders own the manager through Quinbrook Holdings Limited and remain control persons, chair the investment committee and sit on portfolio boards, while Brian Restall and three regional leaders run the firm. Rory Quinlan's resignation from the UK board (18 July 2025) is a seat change, not a departure — he is still Managing Partner, a control person and a Habitat director. Collection gap: the UK company reports 'no ultimate controlling party' while the ADV shows the two founders' vehicles each at 50–75%; the two statements describe the same structure from different legal tests.

**(Low confidence)** We assess that **Frederick County's moratorium is the first material political risk to a Quinbrook platform**, because Rowan's largest campus sits inside the contested overlay zone and the county executive has turned against new development through July 2027. Basis: the Maryland Supreme Court ruling and the September 2026 rejection of the neighbouring Quantum Maryland agreement. Rowan's existing Bauxite phases may be unaffected; no party has said.

**INDICATORS TO WATCH** — *Any Companies House PSC02/PSC07 on Habitat Energy Limited, a TM01 for the Quinbrook directors, or a Quinbrook portfolio-page status change from 'Operational & Expanding':* a completed Habitat sale shows there before any release. *Filing of the FY2025 accounts of Habitat Energy Limited and Renewable and Grid Services Limited:* the group 'Optimisation services' line (GBP 4.17m in FY2024), the going-concern wording and any post-balance-sheet note on the sale. *A Quinbrook release or Form D amendment on Quinbrook III:* the first close and whether the USD 4bn target holds. *Supernode Stage 3 completion (2027) and a Stage 4 / EnerQB decision:* the next battery order the manager itself would sign. *A Rowan 8-K-equivalent or Blackstone filing stating the stake:* would convert the reported 49% into a fact. *Frederick County's July 2027 moratorium end:* whether Rowan's later phases proceed.

relationships.scale: 100% (terms undisclosed); held in QRIF via Renewable and Grid Services Limited
relationships.note: Quinbrook acquired Habitat Energy Limited on 30 November 2021 and holds it through its UK holding group; a sale process was reported in March 2026 and remains unresolved.
relationships.context:
Quinbrook's release of 30 November 2021 records the acquisition; Companies House shows Renewable and Grid Services Limited as Habitat's 75%+ person with significant control from that date, with Scaysbrook, Quinlan and James Allan appointed directors the same day, Hank Jones on 17 June 2025 and Keith Gains on 10 December 2025. RGS's FY2024 group accounts carry Habitat's 'Optimisation services' turnover of GBP 4,169,575 (+80%) and name Quinbrook Holdings Limited as ultimate controlling party.

New Project Media reported on 17 March 2026 that Quinbrook was 'working with JLL and Boston Consulting Group' to sell Habitat; Quinbrook did not comment and no bidder, price, signing or withdrawal has been reported since. Quinbrook's Habitat portfolio page, labelled 'Operational & Expanding', has not been modified since 29 August 2025. On 3 October 2026 both Habitat Energy Limited and RGS showed FY2025 accounts overdue at Companies House. This dossier and `habitat-energy` v3 tell the same story from the two sides.

relationships.scale: 'significant minority stake' in Rowan (reported 49% at ~USD 3.8bn ex-debt); lead LP in the USD 600m Valley of Fire fund

relationships.context:
The joint release of 9 April 2026 states that 'funds affiliated with Blackstone have acquired a significant minority stake in Rowan' and quotes David Scaysbrook as Rowan's chairman; it gives no percentage, price or value basis, and no standalone Blackstone release was located. The Information, via IREI and The Tech Capital, reported 49% at a company valuation of about USD 3.8bn excluding debt with Quinbrook retaining operational control — reported, not announced. Blackstone Digital Infrastructure Trust's Q2 2026 10-Q does not mention Rowan.

The relationship began earlier: Quinbrook's 4 April 2024 release names Blackstone Strategic Partners as lead investor in the USD 600m Valley of Fire continuation fund that bought 51% of Gemini from the first fund.

relationships.context: CATL's and Quinbrook's joint release of 15 August 2026 records CATL's EnerC Plus containers for Supernode Stages 1–2 and TENER S for Stage 3, with a long-term service agreement, and says EnerQB is 'being considered for future stages'. Quinbrook's 5 March 2025 release announced EnerQB, an 8-hour long-duration battery co-developed with CATL and its affiliate Private Energy Partners and named for Quinbrook, with more than 3 GW planned across Quinbrook's Australian sites, the first at Supernode Stage 4. The procurement counterparty in these documents is Quinbrook, not a portfolio company.

relationships.scale: Power conversion and SCADA for Supernode Stages 1–2 (about 1 GWh of Stage 2)
relationships.note: GE Vernova supplied the power-conditioning and controls for Supernode's first two stages, per trade press.
relationships.context: pv magazine Australia reported on 23 September 2024 that Quinbrook selected GE Vernova to supply power conditioning and SCADA for Supernode's 1 GWh second stage, following the first stage's integration; Quinbrook's own releases name the project's lenders and offtakers but not the conversion supplier. The relationship is documented in trade press, not in a first-party release of either company.

relationships.scale: Scout Clean Energy sold for about USD 1bn in cash (binding contracts 29 September 2022)
relationships.note: Brookfield Renewable bought Scout Clean Energy, the US wind platform Quinbrook built from a USD 6m start-up stake, for about USD 1bn in cash.
relationships.context: Quinbrook's release of 30 September 2022 records binding contracts to sell Scout Clean Energy to Brookfield Renewable for 'c. US$1 billion in cash on completion' after Quinbrook's initial USD 6m investment in 2017 and USD 470m of further equity; Scout's own release adds a potential USD 350m of additional near-term investment by Brookfield. The consideration is stated as cash, not as an enterprise value. Brookfield appears in this corpus as a capital-segment incumbent; here it is the buyer of Quinbrook's first flagship exit.

policyExposure.regime: UK National Security and Investment Act 2021 (with Ofgem notification)
policyExposure.exposure: Quinbrook's sale of Flexitricity to Drax was conditional on approval under the NSI Act and notification to Ofgem, both cleared by completion on 31 March 2026; any sale of Habitat Energy, a UK-licensed optimiser, runs the same gate.
policyExposure.mitigation: Quinbrook used the standard mandatory-notification route; no call-in or remedy was reported.

policyExposure.regime: NESO Stability Pathfinder contracts, Contracts for Difference and the Capacity Market (UK)
policyExposure.exposure: Quinbrook's UK revenues are regulated-contract revenues: ten-year CPI-linked Stability Pathfinder contracts on eight synchronous condensers ('more than half of the GBP 323 million total contract value' of Pathfinder II), a 15-year CfD (AR4) and a 15-year Capacity Market agreement at Cleve Hill, and EirGrid's Low Carbon Inertia Services contract at Wexford; QRIF II is pitched on Clean Power 2030.

policyExposure.regime: Local data-centre zoning — Frederick County, Maryland moratorium
policyExposure.exposure: Rowan's Quantum Frederick campuses (Bauxite I–III) sit inside the Critical Digital Infrastructure overlay zone whose expansion was litigated in 2026; after the Maryland Supreme Court blocked a referendum (30 June 2026), the county executive rejected the neighbouring Quantum Maryland agreement and extended a moratorium on new data-centre development to 1 July 2027. Rowan entities were plaintiffs in the April 2026 suits.
policyExposure.mitigation: Rowan signed the White House Ratepayer Protection Pledge (July 2026), committed USD 38m to Temple water infrastructure and published a 'Community Guarantee' (September 2026).

policyExposure.regime: US tax credits — PTC transferability and FEOC restrictions on Primergy's fleet
policyExposure.exposure: Primergy's March 2026 Gemini refinancing is backed by 'a 10-year production tax credit transfer deal', and Gemini was financed with USD 1.9bn of debt and tax equity; changes to transferability or foreign-entity-of-concern rules bear directly on the US solar-plus-storage fleet. Quinbrook's own statement is only that 'shifting US policy' is reshaping investment flows (Scaysbrook, December 2025).

policyExposure.regime: Queensland state development policy and state-owned counterparties
policyExposure.exposure: Quinbrook's Australian pipeline runs through the state: Stanwell Corporation (state-owned) is Supernode's Stage 3 offtaker, bought Lockyer Energy from Quinbrook in 2025 and holds exclusivity on the Gladstone SDA Energy Hub; Powerlink (state-owned) provides the Supernode connection; Northern Quartz is a declared 'prescribed project'. AEMO registers Supernode BESS as a scheduled bidirectional unit with Origin as intermediary.

policyExposure.regime: US Investment Advisers Act — SEC registration and exempt reporting
policyExposure.exposure: Quinbrook Infrastructure Partners LLC is an SEC-registered adviser (801-112447) with the Jersey, UK and Australian entities as exempt reporting advisers; the funds are 3(c)(7) private funds with Luxembourg SCSp parallels (AIFMD marketing). No disciplinary disclosures appear on any Quinbrook ADV. The US Senate letters of 2025–26 on private-equity data-centre ownership do not name Quinbrook.
